# ines: the world the record is a shadow of

The record is not her life. It is what her tools happened to capture, and the
gap between the two is where most engine mistakes live.

## What captures what

- **The watch** records her runs, including their RPE, on the scale her watch
  uses - Borg's 6-20, where an easy run sits at 11 to 13.
- **The strength app** records her Tuesday sets, including their RPE, on the
  scale that app uses - CR10, where a hard set sits at 8.
- **The food app** records energy and protein all day and syncs overnight.
- **The bathroom scale** records a weight by Bluetooth twice a week.
- **She types** the one gym weigh-in herself, and both journal lines.

## The two scales

Her record carries an RPE of 12 on a run and an RPE of 8 on a set, and those
are an easy effort and a hard one respectively. Nothing in the record says so.
The integers are not comparable and there is no field that could tell a reader
that, which is a real hazard in a record whose two sources genuinely differ -
and hers is the only record in this corpus where they do.

This is stated here rather than fixed in the data, because the data is honest:
her tools really do use different scales and really do not say which.

## The gym weigh-in

One reading, on a different scale, after dinner, in clothes. It is 1.4 kg
above the trend and it is not an error - it is a different measurement of a
different thing, and she labelled the procedure honestly rather than dropping
it. A record that only contains comparable readings is a record someone has
already cleaned.

## The achilles

Ten days of a 2, left side, in the middle of the record. It goes once she is
warm, and she says so in the journal. It is not an injury and she did not stop
running; it is the ordinary background noise a real record carries and a
synthetic one usually omits.
